### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19 and A20 have all but stopped running: each took part in about half of the earlier traces (roughly 99 and 103 of 200) but in only 1 and 4 of 200 later traces, and before the change they were near-mutually exclusive alternatives, each appearing without the other in about 49–51 in 100 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, REL009]
- Two activities not seen at all earlier, A25 and A26, now run in about 99 in 100 later traces (198 of 200 each), once per trace; they appear together in about 99 in 100 traces, with A25 first in about half of those and A26 first in the other half. [OCC003, OCC004, REL018]
- The step A42 now routes to the new pair: before, about 42% of its observed outgoing transitions went to A20 and about 40% to A19, with A42 preceding A19/A20 in about half of traces; after, about 43% go to A25 and 41% to A26, on roughly 200 observations per window. [DIR008, REL013, REL017]
- The new pair occupies the old branch's place between A42 and A27: A42 precedes A25/A26 in about 98 in 100 later traces, A25/A26 precede A27 in about 98–99 in 100, the A42-to-A27 distance moved from mostly 2 steps (about 82 in 100) to mostly 3–4 steps (about 78 and 21 in 100), and A27's average position shifted slightly later (about 0.41 to 0.43 of the trace). [REL020, REL022, REL019, REL021, LAG004, POS005]
- The old branch's link to A27 is gone: before, A19 or A20 preceded A27 in about half of traces; after, A27 still runs in every trace but essentially never after A19/A20, and A14 no longer co-occurs with A19/A20 (co-occurrence fell from about half of traces to 2 in 100 or fewer). [REL012, REL016, REL005, REL006]
- Secondary routing redistributions appear downstream: from A06 and A10 the shares reaching A19/A20 disappeared while A25/A26 (and A15, A16, A46) gained, based on modest support of roughly 36–48 outgoing transitions per window; from A07 the share to A05 fell from about 44% to 28% while the share to A14 rose from about 26% to 44%, with the A07-to-A14 gap concentrating at 1 step (about 27% to 44%). [DIR001, DIR003, DIR002, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the alternative pair A19/A20 that each covered about half of the cases is no longer executed, and the new pair A25/A26 now runs in nearly every case on the path between A42 and A27, where A19/A20 previously sat. The participation changes are large and well supported on both sides (about 99–103 of 200 traces before versus 1–4 after for A19/A20, and 0 versus 198 of 200 for A25/A26), which sampling variation in variant frequencies cannot plausibly explain. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

The hypothesis is shown directly rather than by accumulation of items: A42's successors flipped from A19/A20 to A25/A26 on about 200 observations per window, and the relational and lag evidence places A25/A26 after A42 and before A27, with the A42-to-A27 distance growing by about one step. Although many items qualify, they express only a few distinct behavioural differences — the disappearance of A19/A20, the insertion of A25/A26, and the secondary routing shifts — clearly more than the 0.65 items expected by chance in this screening, and the many agreeing relation items reflect the same underlying traces rather than independent confirmations. [DIR008, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, LAG004, OCC003]

Limitations remain: zero participation shows only that A19/A20 were not observed in the later sample, not that they are impossible there, and the evidence cannot fully exclude that the disappearance and the insertion are two independent changes that happen to meet at A42. The smaller shifts — the A05/A14 swap at A07 and parts of the A06/A10 redistribution — are of a size that sampling differences between windows can produce and should not be read as separate changes. [DIR002, DIR001, DIR003, OCC001]
